L-lysine binds to Slc7a1, which is involved in the transport of basic amino acids across cellular membranes. This transporter, Slc7a1, is part of a broader functional pathway that includes Slc7a4. The integration of these relationships implies that L-lysine may influence the activity of Slc7a4 through its interaction with Slc7a1, potentially modulating the transport function of Slc7a4. The observed scores indicate a plausible but not definitive connection, suggesting that further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between L-lysine and Slc7a4. The mechanism appears to involve a transmembrane transport pathway, where L-lysine could act as a regulatory molecule affecting the function of the Slc7a4 transporter.
